issues.legal_issue: A court may award rent or mesne profits accruing during a suit where the defendant’s own position and the payment of the additional court fee establish that the suit includes a claim for ejectment.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought rent and asked that the defendant be required to vacate if provisional rent was not paid.
The defendant objected that the suit was not one for ejectment and that mesne profits during the suit could not be awarded.
The defendant had himself pleaded that the suit was for ejectment, and the plaintiff had paid the additional court fee for an ejectment suit.
issues.conclusion: The objection to awarding rent or mesne profits during the suit was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Order 20, Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and held that, in the circumstances, the defendant could not object to an award of mesne profits on the ground that the suit was not for ejectment. No earlier cases were cited for this ruling.

predicates.ejectment_claim_in_rent_suit: The proceeding sought rent and included a claim that the occupant vacate in specified circumstances.
predicates.defendant_pleaded_suit_was_for_ejectment: The defendant characterized the proceeding as a suit for ejectment.
predicates.additional_ejectment_court_fee_paid: The plaintiff paid the additional court fee applicable to an ejectment suit.

issues.definition: When a rent suit includes an ejectment claim, the defendant characterized it as an ejectment suit, and the additional court fee was paid, the objection to awarding rent or mesne profits during the suit is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: An amount shown by the tenant’s conduct to have been accepted as rent may be treated as the agreed rent and, where the first letting falls after the relevant cutoff, as the basic rent for standard-rent purposes.
material_facts: The High Court relied principally on the tenant’s admission in proceedings before the Custodian and inferred that the tenant was willing to pay the stated monthly rent.
The first letting of the premises was after the cutoff relevant to the first proviso to Section 6(2) of the rent-control statute.
The High Court treated the accepted rent as both the agreed rent and the basic rent.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the stated rent was the agreed rent and the basic rent was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the first proviso to Section 6(2) of the Rajasthan Premises (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1950, to a first letting after the relevant cutoff. It held that the evidence supported the inference that the tenant was willing to pay the rent found by the High Court. No earlier cases were cited for this ruling.

predicates.rent_recovery_or_standard_rent_proceedin: The proceeding concerns recovery of rent or determination of standard rent.
predicates.tenant_acknowledged_willingness_to_pay_a: The tenant’s statement or conduct in related proceedings showed willingness to pay a particular rent.
predicates.initial_letting_was_after_relevant_rent_: The premises were first let after the cutoff relevant to the rent-control rule for determining basic rent.

issues.definition: When a rent or standard-rent proceeding concerns premises first let after the relevant cutoff and the tenant’s conduct shows willingness to pay a particular rent, that rent is treated as the agreed and basic rent.

issues.legal_issue: A receiver appointed to realize rent is competent to sue for rent arrears falling within that authority.
material_facts: The receiver was specifically authorized to realize rent from tenants and to take necessary legal steps to realize arrears.
The receiver’s claim was limited to arrears within the period for which recovery was sought in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The objection to the receiver’s competence to sue for the rent arrears was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the receiver as an officer of the court who realizes income and holds it in trust for the person who ultimately succeeds. The receiver’s express appointment to realize arrears supported the authority to sue. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.rent_arrears_recovery_suit: The proceeding seeks recovery of rent arrears from an occupant.
predicates.receiver_appointed_to_realize_rent_arrea: A receiver was appointed with authority to collect rent and take legal steps to recover arrears.
predicates.arrears_claim_falls_within_receiver_mand: The arrears sought are within the authority given to the receiver.

issues.definition: In a rent-arrears suit, a receiver appointed to collect rent and pursue arrears is competent to sue for arrears within that appointment.

issues.legal_issue: A suit combining rent recovery with standard-rent relief is not defeated by misjoinder or by an objection that standard rent must be pursued separately in another court where the reliefs are linked and the rent recovery can rest on an established agreement.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought recovery of rent and, alternatively, fixation of standard rent in the same suit.
The rent-recovery claim was linked to the standard-rent relief.
The High Court found an agreed rent on which a decree could be based without fixing basic rent.
In an earlier revision in the same suit, the High Court had rejected the objection that standard rent had to be fixed in the Munsiff’s Court.
issues.conclusion: The objections based on misjoinder and the asserted need to bring standard-rent proceedings separately in the Munsiff’s Court were rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reasoned that the rent claim was linked to the standard-rent relief and, in any event, an agreed rent supported a decree without a separate fixation. It also regarded the forum objection as already rejected in the earlier revision in the same suit. No statutory provision or earlier reported case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.rent_recovery_and_standard_rent_claims_j: The plaintiff sought rent recovery and standard-rent relief in the same proceeding.
predicates.claims_are_linked: The rent-recovery relief depended on or was connected with the standard-rent relief.
predicates.agreed_rent_established: The evidence established an agreed rent on which rent recovery could be based without fixing standard rent.
predicates.separate_forum_objection_previously_reje: An earlier ruling in the same proceeding had rejected the objection that standard rent had to be determined in a separate forum.

issues.definition: When rent recovery and standard-rent claims are joined and linked, the combined suit is not defeated by misjoinder or a separate-forum objection if an agreed rent is established or that forum objection was already rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee may recover rent arrears that accrued before the transfer where a contract to the contrary is embodied in the compromise between the parties.
material_facts: The claim included arrears of rent that accrued before the transfer.
The compromise petition, incorporated into the compromise decree, contained an express arrangement contrary to the ordinary rule against a transferee recovering pre-transfer arrears.
issues.conclusion: The transferee was entitled to the pre-transfer arrears under the express arrangement in the compromise.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the proviso to Section 109 of the Transfer of Property Act, holding that a transferee is ordinarily not entitled to rent arrears due before the transfer unless there is a contract to the contrary. It found such a contract in the compromise petition incorporated into the decree. No earlier cases were cited for this ruling.

predicates.rent_claim_after_property_transfer: The proceeding seeks rent after an interest in the property has been transferred.
predicates.arrears_accrued_before_transfer: Some of the rent sought became due before the transfer.
predicates.express_contrary_contract_in_compromise: The parties expressly agreed in a compromise, incorporated into a court decree, that the transferee could recover the earlier arrears.

issues.definition: When a transferee seeks rent that accrued before the transfer and an express contrary agreement is embodied in the parties’ compromise, the transferee is entitled to those arrears.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise agreement recognizing a transfer does not require registration merely because it is embodied in a decree, unless its terms necessarily require execution of a deed of conveyance.
material_facts: The agreement recognizing the transfer was embodied in a compromise decree.
The compromise terms did not provide for execution of a deed of transfer or conveyance.
The defendant argued that the compromise terms required a registered deed to be enforceable.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the compromise required registration was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that an agreement embodied in a compromise decree recognizing a transfer did not require registration unless the terms necessarily involved execution of a deed of conveyance. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.transfer_recognition_embodied_in_comprom: The parties’ agreement recognizing a transfer was incorporated into a compromise decree.
predicates.compromise_does_not_require_conveyance_d: The compromise terms did not require the parties to execute a deed of conveyance.
predicates.registration_is_challenged: A party objected that the compromise agreement could not be enforced without registration.

issues.definition: When a compromise decree recognizes a transfer but does not require execution of a conveyance deed, the agreement is enforceable without registration despite an objection to its registration.
